name: Multiligament Knee Injury
definition: Injury involving two or more major knee ligaments, commonly after high-energy trauma and sometimes associated with knee dislocation.

core: ACL/PCL/collateral stability after acute safety assessment

investigations.principle: MRI defines ligament pattern after stabilization; vascular imaging is dictated by vascular assessment.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Reconstruction timing and staging are individualized by injury pattern, soft tissues and neurovascular status.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-Snayu complex injury phenotype may be documented after emergency assessment.

patientEducation.summary: Injury involving two or more major knee ligaments, commonly after high-energy trauma and sometimes associated with knee dislocation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, sepsis, pathological instability or other listed red flags.
